cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Make Them Your Deputy
cards.instruction: Get someone’s help by defining it as service under your direction.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come organize the picnic as my second-in-command. I'll give you the shopping instructions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm happy to shop, but I'm not ringing you from every aisle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. I'll issue one clear list and you choose the shop. A good deputy needs room to work.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: And if they haven't got what you listed, I'm choosing the replacements.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Choose them. Just show me the bags before we set out and I'll check the picnic supplies are ready. One report at the end, not twenty phone calls. That's the direction I'll give you.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 defines picnic help as second-in-command service; A3 yields shop choice and A5 replacements while preserving one brief and a final report under A check.

relationship.evidence: B2 willingly offers shopping but refuses micromanagement; B4 anticipates stock limits, making concessions practical.

heightening.evidence: A5 reduces many imagined check-ins to one actual report and calls the concession a direction.
